witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 89.1
div.ab: Si quis de libertate sua interpellatus fuerit et timens, ne in seruicium cadat, aliquem de propinquis suis, per quem in seruicium cadere timet, occiderit, scilicet patrem aut matrem, patruelem uel auunculum uel quamlibet huiusmodi propinquitatis personam, ipse qui hoc fecerit, secundum legem Saligam moriatur, et agn[a]cio eius et consanguinitas in seruicium cadat.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 604–605 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Verf. benutzte also einen der ‘Zusatz zur Lex Salica’ überschriebenen Codices; vgl. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. Franc. I 111
The author therefore used one of the codices headed ‘Addition to the Lex Salica’; cf. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. Franc. I 111

div.ab: If anyone has been challenged regarding his freedom and, fearing to fall into servitude, has killed any of his near kin through whom he fears to fall into servitude, namely father or mother, father's brother or mother's brother or any person of such kinship, let him who has done this die according to the Salic law, and let his agnates and blood-relations fall into servitude.
